children: GameStop Corp. (GME, Financials) is selling less but making more money. That's the bizarre scenario leading into the Sept. 8 earnings.
GameStop forecasts second-quarter sales of $780 million to $800 million, down with $972.2 million a year ago. Profit is going the opposite way.
The company is looking for net income of $290 million to $310 million, up from $168.6 million a year ago. But there's a big caveat.
The gains included about $238 million from GameStop's investment in eBay, while online assets accounted for a loss of about $75 million.
So the headline profit figure won't tell the real story. What matters more is if GameStop's core company is getting healthier as it closes locations, trims expenses and moves into collectibles.

The corporation had previously achieved record first-quarter operating income earlier this year.Sept. 8 will tell if that improvement is a real trend or if investment gains are still doing most of the work.

title: GameStop Earnings Put Its Profit Turnaround to the Test
